title: Frederik Andersen’s status still a mystery, signs point to Brandon Bussi as Canes Game 5 starter
content:
RALEIGH, N.C. — All signs point to Brandon Bussi making his second straight start for the Carolina Hurricanes on Thursday night in Game 5 of the Stanley Cup Final against the Vegas Golden Knights.

Frederik Andersen, the Hurricanes’ No. 1 throughout the postseason until not dressing in Game 4, didn’t take part in Carolina’s morning skate on Thursday. Bussi was tending his position in what’s deemed to be the starter’s crease.

Coach Rod Brind’Amour said Andersen skated on his own before the team on Thursday and that “everybody’s available.” He wouldn’t discuss the lineup, what’s going on with Andersen or if he’d be backing up on Thursday any further.

If Andersen was going to start or back up, not taking part in the morning skate was extremely abnormal.

Andersen, who has allowed 12 goals in the series, was pulled after giving up four in the second period of Game 3 on Saturday. Bussi came in and stopped 18 of 19 shots before losing in double overtime. He started Game 4 and backstopped Carolina to a 5-3 victory.

Andersen gave up those four goals after getting hit in the head by Ivan Barbashev on an eventual overturned goal by Jack Eichel, so it’s unclear if he’s hurt or continues to need a break, as Brind’Amour said he did after Andersen didn’t dress for Tuesday’s game in Las Vegas.

“It was about a minute conversation with (goalie coach Paul Schonfelder). He said Freddie needs a little break. OK. So we went with the other guy,” Brind’Amour explained after the game. “And if you’re going to give (Andersen) a break, you need to give him a break. So to me, him dressing and going through all that, that’s not really giving him a night off.”

Andersen hasn’t skated with the team since Game 3.

This has been a difficult couple of weeks for Andersen. His friend, mentor and agent, former NHLer Claude Lemieux, died by suicide on May 28. Andersen, in an emotional start, closed out the Montreal Canadiens in the conference finals a day after finding out about Lemieux. Lemieux’s funeral was this past Monday in North Carolina, but Andersen was unable to attend because he was in Las Vegas.

Bussi became the third goaltender in NHL history to make his first career playoff start in a Stanley Cup Final and pick up a win in the contest. The others were Hank Bassen in 1961 for the Detroit Red Wings and Alfie Moore in 1938 with the Chicago Black Hawks.

Bussi won 25 of his first 29 NHL starts, putting up a .901 save percentage in that span, but Andersen regained the starting job by the start of the postseason. Game 3 was the first game action Bussi had seen since April 14.

“He’s been rolling with punches. He’s prepared for this moment for almost two months,” Hurricanes defenseman Shayne Gostisbehere said of Bussi on Thursday. “He’s a pretty easy guy to talk to — calm, cool and collected. I think that (trickles) down from Freddie, too. Freddie’s a lead-by-example guy. You never know his emotions. He’s a calm, cool, collected guy, as well. So it’s good to see Bussi getting the opportunity.”

Bussi’s first opportunity of the season came on Oct. 10, when he stopped 16 of 17 shots in a 5-1 win over the San Jose Sharks. With that performance, Brind’Amour said, Bussi earned an early bit of confidence.

“(He) made some big saves at real big moments of the game,” Brind’Amour said. “We were pretty much in control. But all of a sudden there was a couple Grade-A chances, and he shut the door. And then we went on to win. And then he did the next start, and the next start.

“So obviously there’s a guy that was given an opportunity. Everyone always talks about opportunity, but you gotta do something with it. And he’s done nothing but earn every start that he’s had.”
